The plan's pinned Lean Challenge Statement for stepOk/stepOk_sound types the world argument as World (Fin 4) (LS (Fin 4) Nat) (Msg Nat). That signature is UNIMPLEMENTABLE: Distsys.Exec.Net N M = Packet N M -> Prop has no Decidable instance, so deliver's w.net.mem p premise cannot be decided from a World. The same plan's Decision 4 and report 02 Finding 3 say the opposite -- 'an executable SimWorld mirror with an abstraction into World, NOT decide over World'. The two are in direct conflict; Decision 4 was followed and stepOk takes the mirror, with the pinned CONCLUSION recovered unchanged at ew.toWorld. Nothing is weakened, but the pinned block's argument type is departed from and needs a user ruling.

Distsys.Bracha.applyLabel, which the plan's pinned stepOk_sound names as the successor-world function, is the IDENTITY on .env (.drop _), .env (.duplicate _) and .env (.corrupt _ _) -- its own book needed only the inject case. The plan's run 2 (crash below the bound) drops a crashed node's in-flight packets, so a checker stated over that applier could never accept it. Resolution: a checker-local total applier Distsys.Replay.applyLbl that agrees with Bracha.applyLabel wherever that one is not identity-on-env (proved as applyLbl_eq_applyLabel) and additionally pins the three further byzAllowed cases that ARE deterministic. tamper, the only nondeterministic action, stays outside the alphabet.

Plan Phase 2's negative control B (admit the other room's seats into grv2_project_notes's membership filter via bs._project_accepted) cannot actually produce a cross-ROOM leak: group_rooms.Store.notes(room, ...) is already scoped by room key at the SQL layer, independent of the seat filter, so admitting a foreign seat into room A's membership set never makes room B's physically-stored row appear in room A's query. Implemented instead: group_rooms.Store.notes patched to ignore its room argument and answer with room B's key regardless, with OWNER (the member who sits in both rooms) saving the probe note in room B -- this is the only mechanism that actually demonstrates a cross-room leak, and it exercises exactly the case the plan's own Finding 4 flags as most dangerous (the shared member whose _ch_seat is identical in both rooms).

ControlDMultiRoomLoad concurrency test in tests/test_group_rooms_isolation.py flaked intermittently (docs_rows hit count 1-2 instead of 0) under full-file pytest runs. Root cause: brain_server.py module-level _recl dict (debounced background recluster timers) is never reset by wipe_store / Base.setUp file wipes, so each setUp accept()-driven drain (THIRD note landing in OWNER) arms or extends a timer for the reused OWNER token; across this file several test methods in one pytest process the timer can fire mid-test on a daemon thread and call docs_rows, a pre-existing cross-test global-state leak unrelated to cross-project isolation.
